UNetbootin adds its own bootloader to the usb, give this a try instead:

First run lsblk with the USB drive plugged in and find its name.

Then run this command replacing sdx with the name of the USB drive from the last command and the iso with the tails iso:

TL;DR It sounds like you may need to flash an update to your firmware because the BIOS the computer shipped with had a few bugs.

  • Download it here - make sure to choose "Others" for the OS as BIOS does not apply to an OS.

You want the most recent version (highest number) for your model. I believe that to be the item labeled "BIOS 210 (X202E)". You will also need the BIOS flashing utilities on that page.

FLASHING YOUR BIOS CAN BE DANGEROUS, MAKE SURE YOU FOLLOW THE INSTRUCTIONS FROM ASUS EXACTLY. IF YOU HAVE A QUESTION ABOUT ONE OF THE STEPS, ASK BEFORE YOU DO IT. Although, these things have gotten better lately (usually there is a second, back-up BIOS that can be loaded if something bad happens with the first), it's important to follow all of their instructions.

Before you go out and do any of this, do the following:

  1. Tell us the current version of your BIOS.
  2. Link us the TAILS page that recommends BIOS changes for this laptop. (or list them out)
  3. Double triple check those BIOS settings.

Can you get any usb running from your computer? Have you tried the legacy settings? Is your boot device eufi compatible? You may also want to try another USB. I don't know why but I have a usb drive that just will not boot.
